instruction: Write a detailed, high-quality model answer to this career-motivation question. Stay within approximately 300 words and do not invent employers, degrees, or authorities beyond those permitted.
input: Please outline why you wish to pursue a career in commercial law? (approx. 300 words max)
output:
My interest in commercial work grew from seeing how businesses operate under pressure. While at M&S during a period of financial difficulty in the retail sector, I saw the challenges firms can face day to day. At a take-away, rising local competition led me to set up a Facebook page as a low-cost way to advertise. That change reduced fact-checking calls, let me serve customers more quickly, and improved satisfaction—deepening my interest in the competitive yet rewarding side of business.

Volunteering at Citizens Advice for several months, advising clients, then confirmed that I would enjoy an advisory role solving both commercial and legal problems. A career in commercial law also follows naturally from my International Relations degree: I liked working with different theories and turning them into persuasive arguments, and I am drawn to analysing large volumes of information to reach practical conclusions for clients. I also want a challenging environment. Citizens Advice gave me insight into the responsibility and everyday pressures of lawyer-like work. The chance to keep adapting, learning, and growing—personally and professionally—is what has solidified my wish to pursue commercial law.
generation_notes: Detailed motivation rewrite; M&S, take-away/Facebook, Citizens Advice, IR only.
